summary: Bloomberg reports that SAP is preparing an AI-era restructuring that could eliminate at least 10,000 positions, roughly 9% of its global workforce, with product development, engineering and sales in particular focus. This is preliminary, journalist-reported planning based on unnamed sources, not a company-confirmed announcement or completed layoffs. The total could change after labour negotiations; it is not a count of proven direct AI replacements.
evidenceQuote: The total number of job cuts hasn’t been finalized and might still change after labor negotiations, they added.
notes: Bloomberg reporting was read in full via The Hindu BusinessLine. November 26 is the reporting date, not a confirmed company announcement date. Sources familiar with the plans link them to CEO Christian Klein’s AI-first strategy and changes in how SAP develops and sells products. SAP said it continuously reviews its organization but declined to comment on planned cuts. The numeric value 10,000 is the reported preliminary lower bound, not completed departures or a final negotiated total. Around 9% is the reported global workforce share, not an AI-attributable subset. Germany has an employment guarantee through 2028, according to the report; this is not a Germany-only reduction. This new 2026 proposal is separate from the January 2024 restructuring already tracked; that earlier round is not counted again here. Verified status describes the sourced report, not confirmation that the proposal will proceed.

sources.name: Bloomberg via The Hindu BusinessLine: SAP weighs 10,000 job cuts amid AI-first strategy
